newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Lee calls for cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Lee calls for cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui has asked Premier Lien Chan to reshuffle his cabinet next week, a senior official said on Wednesday.

"I have retained Premier Lien Chan...I have asked Lien Chan to make some adjustments in cabinet," Wu Poh-hsiung, ruling Nationalist Party secretary-general, quoted Lee as saying at the party's central standing committee meeting.

Wu said Lien tendered his resignation on Sunday to take responsibility for the government's failure to check violent crime, an issue which came under intense scrutiny following the murder of a popular actress' teenage daughter.
"The top priority is to resolve the case," Wu quoted Lee as saying.
The premier would give his reshuffle list for approval during next Wednesday's central standing committee meeting.

Taiwanese were shocked by last week's discovery of the body of 17-year-old Pai Hsien-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping. Her kidnappers, who dumped her naked body in a river, have not been caught. More than 50,000 people demonstrated on Sunday to demand the resignation of Lien and a cabinet reshuffle.
